- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low, true outcome often overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment is bullish.
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts in early horizon (e.g., 10–15 days ahead); apply sentiment-weighted smoothing to early forecast segments.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often misses momentum — add 0.5–1.5% lagged momentum to forecast.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — if sentiment >0.67 and price rises >5% from prior, cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
